built.label: fig:pipeline-status
built.note: Four stages numbered 1 to 4 as Chapter 1 numbers them. Every number is read by key from results/accord/VERIFIED_FACTS.json (keys: gold.base_rate_299, gold.n_total, exemplar.rule_1_2_pooled_exemplar_correct_rate_in_299.rate, exemplardirect.defect_rate, exemplar_recomputed.rule_1_2_pooled.wrong_rate, c120.g299.n, c120.g299.n_flagged, c120.g299.mcc, c120.g299.ceiling_mcc, rulehead.test_rule_type_macro_f1, decontam.aggregate.ensemble_auroc, decontam.aggregate.ensemble_ci95_hi, sizectl108.power_curves.primary_crossing_power_0_80); no withdrawn key is readable. Every number on the canvas prints to two decimals, except stage 1's three miss rates, which print to four as the captions do; full precision stays in this note and in the tables. Three chip encodings, distinct in greyscale and named in an on-canvas key: stage 1 not established (MIST fill under a heavy dashed GRAPHITE rim, 1.7pt, with no hatch and no edge bar; miss rate at least 0.4364, the displayed-exemplar lower bound read as 72 of 165 from results/accord/clinical_core/displayed_exemplar_lower_bound.json, against readings of 0 and 0.9315 from the other two instruments; the verdict does not move, because a lower bound does not pin the rate); stages 2 and 3 reading unsupported (solid scarlet, the only scarlet on the canvas: MCC 0.0269 against a ceiling of 0.0780; the three credited architectural components fail a code audit); stage 4 bounded null (paper fill, solid rim: interval upper end 0.7034 under the 80 percent power floor 0.7466). The carrier rail is GRAPHITE, not scarlet: it records that stages 2 to 4 consumed the exemplar stage 1 selected, which is shared input, not a failed check. No plate; the stage column is sized from measured text widths so the spine takes about the left fifth of the canvas. No internal identifiers on the canvas.

built.label: fig:exemplar
built.note: Five readings of one quantity, the share of Rules 1 and 2 candidates whose displayed exemplar is wrong, on one axis. Four are on the 165 annotated pairs and are ordered by how many of those pairs each instrument excludes; the fifth, under a hairline, is on the 1,307 rebuilt candidates and shares no row with them. Every rate is a count over a denominator read from results/accord/VERIFIED_FACTS.json by key (exemplar_recomputed.rule_1_2_pooled.n, exemplar_recomputed.rule_1_2_pooled.n_wrong, exemplar_recomputed.rule_1_2_pooled.n_resolved, exemplar_recomputed.rule_1_2_pooled.n_unresolved, exemplar.rule_1_2_pooled_exemplar_correct_rate_in_299.n_known, exemplar.rule_1_2_pooled_exemplar_correct_rate_in_299.n_correct, exemplardirect.n_wrong, exemplardirect.n_decidable, exemplardirect.n_undecidable, exemplardirect.n_wrong_involves_unclassified, c129.pooled.positional_outside_trigger_set.either_side.count, c129.pooled.positional_outside_trigger_set.either_side.n), except the displayed-exemplar lower bound, which has no register key yet and is read as two counts from results/accord/clinical_core/displayed_exemplar_lower_bound.json (72 of 165). No rate is typed. Every interval is a Wilson interval recomputed here from the row's own two counts and asserted against the interval the artifact stores. The SCARLET_TINT band is the union of the three low-exclusion intervals, computed on the canvas, and the headline prints its ends (0.3630 to 0.5576); the assertion that the high reading's lower end (0.8785) clears that union fails the build if the cluster ever dissolves. Open marks, not a second hue, mark the two readings their own analysis limits: the direct extractor (69 of its 136 defect rows have no classified action on at least one side) and the key join (23 rows resolved of 165). Rules 3 and 4 are named on the canvas and drawn nowhere: the artifact tags both defect_interpretation none, which this generator asserts. No clinical text, no identifiers, no pair identifiers on the canvas.

built.label: fig:cohort-flow
sources: results/accord/source_summaries/phase1_summary.json, derived: has_both_roles 9820 minus valid_admissions_both_selected 9783; admissions holding both note roles for which no nursing note has a non-null chart time strictly before discharge
built.note: Path from the source database to the evaluated core, ten stages. Every count is read from results/accord/VERIFIED_FACTS.json by key (cohort.heart_failure.pre_los, cohort.heart_failure.post_los, cohort.heart_failure.removed, cohort_chain.has_both_roles, cohort_chain.valid_admissions_both_selected, cohort_chain.both_roles_not_selectable, extraction.medication_extraction.total_mentions, extraction.medication_extraction.classified_mentions, extraction.medication_extraction.unclassified_derived, extraction.temporal_prefilter.final_candidates, extraction.annotation_sample.total_sampled, c120.g299.n, c120.g299.n_positives, c120.g253.n, c120.g253.n_positives, overcallamb.n_ambiguous), and every right-hand count carries its unit. Every stub under the 'left the path' heading states an exclusion, never a kept count (audit item 5), except the one at the temporal prefilter, which carries no count: solid stubs are exclusions the register records as counts (11 with no positive length of stay, 37 with no nursing note before discharge, 131,347 unclassified mentions, 46 coded ambiguous). Dashed stubs are drops no file records as an exclusion, drawn as differences computed in code from two register counts: admissions after the length-of-stay filter minus admissions with both note types (3777); candidates minus the sample (1,678); the sample minus the annotated pairs (1). The dashed stub at the temporal prefilter used to print mentions with an action class minus candidates as a count of dropped mentions. A candidate is a pair of mentions matched under a rule, so that difference mixed units and is no longer computed or drawn; the stub now says in italic that the unit changes from mentions to candidates, and the two registered counts (88,336 mentions, 1,978 candidates) stand in their stage boxes. The ambiguous count is read from overcallamb.n_ambiguous, asserted equal to 299 minus 253 and cross-checked against the signal-check file. The core is drawn in the pharmacist's emerald rather than scarlet, which the set reserves for a failed check. Headline built from the register: of 1,978 candidates, 12 contradictions survive sampling and annotation.

built.label: fig:prevalence-response
built.note: Built by fig_batch2.make_fig_prevalence_response(). Rates and Wilson intervals from the sweep artifact; the register mirrors the maximum over-call cell (publicsweep.results.*.over_call_ratio), and overcall.qwen3_8b.pool.ratio and overcall.llama3_8b.pool.ratio are read to assert the public maximum sits below the clinical range and to print the clinical maximum in the deck. One hue per public model, from style.PUBLIC_MODEL_MARK: llama3:8b MAGENTA, circle, solid; granite3.3:8b VIOLET, square, dash (0,(4,2)); qwen3:8b CYAN, triangle, dot (0,(1,1.5)); line and interval in the ramp's DEEP, marker face in its CORE. granite3.3:8b was TANGERINE until the visual audit, which read it as the detector ensemble's AMBER (9.7 dE76 apart at DEEP); VIOLET is 104.5 from AMBER at DEEP and is used for nothing else. The shared legend prints the tables' display names (Llama 3 8B, Granite 3.3 8B, Qwen 3 8B) from style.PUBLIC_MODEL_NAME, not the registry tags. Series are dodged by -0.004, 0, +0.004 on x so intervals do not overprint; the dodge is a drawing offset and all three models were run at the same four prevalence levels. ylim -0.012 to 0.32, xlim 0 to 0.30; the gutter between the panels is 22pt so the end tick labels of the two x axes do not read as one number. The over-prediction wedge is MIST and the calibration diagonal is labelled in both panels.

built.label: fig:power
built.note: Built by fig_batch2.make_fig_power(). Keys: power.n_positives, power.n_negatives, power.alpha, power.power, sizectl108.power_curves.n_pos_slots, n_neg_slots, mde_analytic, primary_crossing_power_0_80, label_mix.crossings_at_power_0_80.mw_two_sided, label_mix.crossings_at_power_0_80.c98_rule. The Hanley and McNeil curve is recomputed and asserted equal to the register's analytic value. The curve is BOUND_DEEP (COBALT). The region ABOVE the curve is MIST and named on the canvas 'shaded: detectable at 80 percent power'; the region under it is bare paper and named 'not detectable at 80 percent power'. Until the visual audit the shaded side was the one under the curve, the opposite of the forest's bands; both figures now shade what is detectable, in MIST. Three points at 12 positives, each with a leader and a four-decimal label: the analytic value 0.7355, an open COBALT ring on the curve and on the guide; the registered decision rule's simulated floor 0.8084, an INK diamond on the guide; the Mann-Whitney simulated floor 0.7466, an INK disc pulled about 8pt right of the guide and tied back to it by a hairline at its own height, because at the same x it printed on the ring. 0.6 pt SLATE guide at the study's positive count; chance line labelled; ticks 10, 100, 1,000.

built.note: Built by fig_batch2.make_fig_forest(). Keys: decontam.n, decontam.n_positives, decontam.aggregate.ensemble_auroc, ensemble_ci95_lo, ensemble_ci95_hi, c114.task_c.n, n_pos, stratum_auroc, ci95_lo, ci95_hi, c120.g299.n, n_positives, mcc, ceiling_mcc, p_hypergeom_one_sided, c120.g253.n, sizectl108.power_curves.primary_crossing_power_0_80, n_pos_slots, power.power, mde_recomputed.rules34_ambiguous_dropped.minimum_detectable_auc. Row labels are built from these counts. The AUROC axis is shaded MIST per row from that row's own floor to 1, and a two-line note above the panel says what the shading is: 'Shaded: detectable at 80 percent power', then the two named floors, the simulated Mann-Whitney floor 0.7466 at 12 positives for the top row and the analytic floor 0.8064 at 6 positives for the Rules 3 and 4 row. The power figure shades the same kind of region in the same tone. The canvas grew 0.07in in height for the note's second line and both panels moved down 0.08in into bare paper; both keep their size. The MCC zero line is labelled no association. Ensemble in AMBER DEEP/CORE, deployed labeller in PLUM_DEEP. Values print to two decimals.

built.label: fig:ceiling
built.note: Built by fig_ceiling.make_fig_ceiling(). Keys: gold.n_total, gold.base_rate_299, gold.weaklabel_contradiction, exemplar.power_analysis.n_positives_total, c120.g299.n, n_positives, n_flagged, mcc, ceiling_mcc, c120.g253.n, feasgate.n_attaining_their_ceiling and the feasgate.*.ceiling_mcc mirrors. The identity is re-evaluated at every committed gate row and asserted equal to its committed ceiling. The four attaining squares are still checked but no longer drawn (the critique allowed labelling or dropping them; four labels did not fit without crossing a curve). Curves are named at their left ends in the enlarged panel, 12 of 299 and 12 of 253, from the register. The two ceilings are COBALT, solid 1.8pt for the 299-pair basis and dashed 1.2pt for the 253-pair basis. The left panel's y axis runs to 1.07 above a last tick of 1.0, so the peak, which is 1 at the pharmacist's own rate, clears the top spine instead of being drawn on it. The region above both ceilings is COBALT_WASH, runs to the frame, and is labelled not attainable on either basis: the identity defines it. Zoom box 0.6 pt SLATE on all sides (left panel limits widened slightly so no edge sits on a spine). Right panel y label 'Largest attainable MCC (enlarged)'. MCC to two decimals. The scope sentence (a thresholded decision, not a swept score) moved from the deck to the caption.

built.label: fig:scale-ladder
built.note: One model family, one identical prompt, the same 299 annotated pairs, four sizes with a rate and one excluded. Every rate is recomputed here from the cell's own raw_yes_count over n_parsed and asserted against the rate and the Wilson interval the artifact stores; nothing is typed. The excluded rung is Qwen 3 4B, 299 of 299 replies unparseable: it is drawn as a dashed rule with its count and carries no value, and the series segment that spans it is dashed for the same reason. The reference line is the pharmacist base rate, gold.base_rate_299, in the pharmacist's EMERALD; MIST fills everything above it, which is over-calling, as MIST fills the over-prediction wedge on fig-prevalence-response. The fitted slope and r are printed as a note read from the artifact's ladder block and NO fitted line is drawn: the axis stops at the largest size that was run and the figure does not extrapolate. Post hoc descriptive, asserted from the artifact's own note key. No hosted model appears; the family is open-weights.

built.label: fig:answer-polarity
built.note: Three open-weights labellers at one size, the same 299 pairs, two prompts asking complementary questions and differing in nothing else. x is the yes rate to the contradiction question and y the yes rate to the consistency question, both recomputed from raw_yes_count over n_parsed and asserted against the stored rates. The axes box is square in INCHES, so the x plus y equals 1 reference really is a 45 degree line and the distance below it can be read as a distance. The MIST corridor under that line is the share of pairs the pharmacist coded ambiguous, overcallamb.n_ambiguous over gold.n_total, asserted equal to 299 minus 253: a pair can be neither contradictory nor consistent, so that corridor needs no explanation and nothing on this canvas is called logically impossible. Kappa between the two framings is printed as a caveat, not as a claim, because complementary marginals are not per-pair coherence. Post hoc descriptive, asserted from the artifact's own note key.
